NVDA.headline: Substrate supply deals and SpaceX debt claims in focus
NVDA.summary: Reports say NVIDIA, AMD and Intel have reportedly paid over $5 billion to Taiwanese substrate makers to reserve capacity, and Korean reports suggest NVIDIA is backing Samsung's substrate expansion. Elon Musk says SpaceX closed a $40 billion debt deal for AI chips, though sources told Bloomberg pricing talks are ongoing. Shares are at 210.96 USD, down 0.59% today and 6.06% over one month, and up 13.26% over one year.

MSFT.headline: Tesco reportedly moving to Proxmox; Xbox-Netflix deal fell through
MSFT.summary: A Tesco job advert suggests the retailer is replacing VMware with Proxmox, though the report is unofficial and Hyper-V use is only speculation. Puck reported that Xbox sought $800 million from Netflix for game adaptation rights, and the deal has reportedly fallen through, with neither company confirming details. Shares are at 524.51 USD, up 0.66% today, up 5.34% over one month and 0.17% over one year.

AAPL.headline: Market value back at top; iPhone Duo display cracking reports
AAPL.summary: Reports say Apple regained the title of the world's most valuable listed company on 23 October, at about $5.1 trillion, around the iPhone Duo launch. Separate reports describe cracks forming on new iPhone Duo inner displays, with Apple yet to respond officially and no independent failure-rate data. Management changes in display and hardware teams were also reported. Shares are at 347.73 USD, down 0.14% today, up 3.52% over one month and 32.31% over one year.

GOOGL.headline: Aachen injunction over AI Mode; YouTube AV2 plans
GOOGL.summary: A German court reportedly issued a provisional injunction against Google over AI Mode search statements, with fines of up to €250,000 per violation. YouTube plans to roll out the AV2 codec from early 2027, starting on the web. Malaysia may extend its Waze ban from officials to the public, though Google Maps remains legal. Shares are at 320.21 USD, down 1.24% today and 6.47% over one month, and up 23.2% over one year.

AMZN.headline: Japan contractor dismissals; AI servers reportedly awaiting power
AMZN.summary: A Business and Human Rights Centre summary says an Amazon contractor in Japan dismissed 50 staff after offering relocation to Malaysia or termination, though no company response is included. Yahoo Finance reports some newly installed AI servers are reportedly waiting on power, with 29 October cited as a date to show progress. Shares are at 248 USD, down 0.95% today and 0.55% over one month, and up 10.61% over one year.

META.headline: Indian cartoonist posts restricted; AI funding concerns weigh
META.summary: Instagram accounts of Indian cartoonists were reportedly restricted, with Meta citing India's IT Rules without giving specific reasons. Meta's announcement that it needs to raise more money for AI reportedly weighed on its shares and the wider market on Thursday. Instagram also launched as a standalone app on Apple TV. Shares are at 642.62 USD, down 0.96% today, down 17.36% over one month and down 12.97% over one year.

AVGO.headline: Tesco reportedly moving from VMware to Proxmox; VMware litigation ongoing
AVGO.summary: A Tesco job advert suggests the retailer is replacing VMware with Proxmox across its store and edge estate, according to The Register. The Register also reports an ongoing court dispute between Tesco and VMware, with hearings likely in 2027. The shares are down 0.48% today, 8.19% over one month and 9.16% over one year, trading at 321.68 USD within a 52-week range of 289.96–495.

TSLA.headline: Musk political spending, Tesla–SpaceX merger reports and Robotaxi expansion
TSLA.summary: Reports cover Elon Musk's large political donations ahead of the 3 November midterms, including over $76m to America PAC in early October, and a Financial Times piece on a proposed Tesla–SpaceX merger, with no deal terms available. Tesla's Robotaxi service has expanded in Austin to COTA with longer hours, and a Finimize item says Tesla and Nvidia are reportedly backing Samsung's AI chip substrate push, though it is unverified. The shares are down 0.63% today and 1.51% over one month, trading at 372.22 USD.

TSM.headline: Substrate capacity reports and strong one-year gain
TSM.summary: Reports say NVIDIA, AMD and Intel have paid over $5 billion to Taiwanese substrate makers to secure long-term capacity, with substrate supply described as tight. Intel's executives said it is only a few percent behind TSMC on performance but slower to catch up on scale. An EM tech commentary noted volatility in semiconductor stocks. Shares are at 418.51 USD, up 1.49% today, down 7.23% over one month and up 41.89% over one year.

SPCX.headline: Limited news; Safari layout fix under review by Apple
SPCX.summary: There is no major company news in the items provided. Apple is reportedly exploring a fix for Safari's cramped layout on the iPhone Duo's outer display, and Nike has relaunched a boot, which has little bearing on the company. Shares are at 147.49 USD, up 1.89% today, down 0.36% over one month and down 8.36% over one year.

JPM.headline: No major news right now
JPM.summary: There are no recent stories or headlines for JPMorgan Chase. The shares are down 1.47% today and 2.06% over one month, but up 10.36% over one year, trading at 331.58 USD within a 52-week range of 279.1–366.5.
